title: Processing Form Data
description: Handle GET and POST requests, save data, and redirect after success.

slides.title: The POST‑Redirect‑GET Pattern 🔄
slides.content:
After a successful form submission, you should **redirect** the user to a new page (e.g., a success page or the detail page). This prevents duplicate submissions if the user refreshes the page.

Django provides `redirect()` for this purpose.

slides.title: Complete Form Handling Example

quizData.question: Why should you redirect after a successful POST?
options: To prevent duplicate form submissions on refresh
quizData.explanation: Redirecting after POST ensures that refreshing the page doesn't resubmit the form.

slides.title: Handling GET Requests with Data
File Uploads 📎
slides.content:
To handle file uploads, set `enctype="multipart/form-data"` in the form tag and use `request.FILES` in the view.

```python
class UploadForm(forms.Form):
    file = forms.FileField()

# View
if request.method == 'POST':
    form = UploadForm(request.POST, request.FILES)
    if form.is_valid():
        uploaded_file = request.FILES['file']
        # process file
```

ModelForms with `FileField` or `ImageField` handle this automatically.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `get_object_or_404` for editing existing objects

In an update view, retrieve the object first, then pass it as `instance=obj` to the ModelForm to pre‑populate the form.
